title: Security & Compliance Review - Crown & Harbor Insurance
summary: Insurance customer flagged a strict UK data residency requirement: prompts/outputs and derived logs cannot leave the UK. Discussed Private deployment and UK region options.
next_steps: Redwood to confirm availability of UK-only hosting and what telemetry leaves region
Customer to share their residency policy language
transcript:
Meeting: Security & Compliance Review - Crown & Harbor Insurance
Date: 2025-02-11
Duration: 52 min

[00:00] Chloe (Redwood): Thanks everyone. This is our security review. Hiro is here for the deep technical bits.
[00:12] Sophie (Crown&Harbor): Great. Well go down our questionnaire.

[02:40] Ben (Crown&Harbor): First, data residency. We have a hard UK-only requirement for this product line.
[02:49] Chloe: Okay. When you say UK-only, you mean storage, processing, and logs?
[02:56] Ben: Yeah, all of it. Prompts and completions cannot leave the UK, and any derived telemetry cant either.

[05:20] Imran (Crown&Harbor): Some vendors say well process in EU but support is US, and then stuff ends up outside. Weve been burned.
[05:34] Hiro (Redwood): Understood. For Private, its deployed into your VPC, so network egress is under your control. For hosted/dedicated, we can pin regions, but we need to be precise about control plane metadata and support access.

[11:10] Sophie: Do you have SOC 2 Type II?
[11:14] Chloe: Yes, we do. Well provide the report under NDA.

[16:45] Ben: On audit logs, we need them retained in the UK and exported to our SIEM.
[16:58] Hiro: Thats a common setup. Private makes it simplest. We also have export hooks.

[28:30] Sophie: SSO, SAML, SCIM?
[28:34] Chloe: Supported.

[44:10] Imran: If we go hosted, can you guarantee UK region for inference?
[44:18] Chloe: We need to confirm the exact region availability and contract language. It sounds like Dedicated in-region or Private are better fits.

[51:20] Chloe: Recap: UK-only residency is the key gating item. Well follow up with specifics on what can be guaranteed and options.
